page.layout: One column of italic verse, left-aligned with indented lines, in four stanzas plus a printer's ornament at the foot (not text, not transcribed). Running head at top left, page number at top right.

l.i: Vultus, per agros pax nitet aurea,
Et vis facessit. Cana iterum fides

page.notes: Printer's ornament at the foot of the page, not transcribed. "Lary" in line 2 of stanza 1 is doubtful: the letter after "Lar" looks like j or y (read as Larj[?]; the expected form is Lari). "fororcs." in stanza 3 is doubtful; the final letters are not clear and may be "fores" or "sorores". "cecæ" in stanza 5 is doubtful; the ligature may be æ or a. Long s is read as s throughout ("fecuras" read as "securas", "reuifit" as "reuisit"); the word "Quae" in stanza 4 has an unclear ligature.
